title: AI is turning Apple's app review process into a nightmare for synth developers
lede: Synth Anatomy reports that Apple's App Store review, swamped by AI-built apps, now holds iOS music apps for weeks and rejects some for reasons that look automated and wrong.

points: An estimated 10 to 20 new iOS music apps appear daily as people vibe code apps and AUv3 plugins.
Apple says it usually reviews 90% of submissions within 48 hours; developers report weeks with no updates.
Unfiltered Audio's app was rejected four times, once over an invented licensing requirement, and shipped without its MIDI version.
CRUX Synth was rejected four times as design spam within seconds of entering review, and its appeals went unanswered.
Pittsburgh Modular's iOS synth arrived more than two weeks after its planned simultaneous VST release.

points.text: Developers outside music report the same: one client app was asked for a full video walkthrough, then sat unreviewed for over a week.
Some say review was poor long before AI, and the blame lies with Apple alone.
One developer finds Google Play worse, citing a rule requiring 12 testers for 14 days; a reply notes Apple's fee recurs every year.
Another says Anthropic's MCP directory review is slower still, after eight months of resubmissions.
